title: Using Emerging EBSD and TKD Tools for Phase Detection in Martensitic Steels
content: The goal of this work is to develop techniques for the consistent quantitative measurement of microstructural features in martensitic steels using electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD) and transmitted Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) techniques. EBSD is a powerful technique for phase detection in crystalline materials [1], and has been used successfully to study both small microstructural features [2] and to differentiate between phases in multiphase steels [3]. Here we study 10 wt% Ni (10Ni) steel, a structural steel that is primarily martensitic. The steel undergoes a quench, lamellarization, and temper heat treatment for optimal mechanical properties. This produces a microstructure that is primarily martensitic with a small fraction of both globular grains and films of retained austenite (RA). These features are on the order of 10s to hundreds of nm in size such that the smaller RA features are close to the spatial resolution limitations of EBSD at accelerating voltages of 10 – 30 kV. Thus, inconsistent measurements of RA phase fractions are often obtained using conventional EBSD techniques. Non-local pattern averaging reindexing (NLPAR) is a method to denoise EBSD or TKD patterns while maintaining sharp boundaries and small features [4]. Here as-collected and NLPAR denoised patterns have been indexed using a vendor Hough technique, a recently developed radon approach as implemented in the Python package PyEBSDIndex [5], and the spherical indexing (SI) [6, 7] approach.
